subproblem.title: The graph map x -> y + q(graphPoint x (v x)) is C^1 with derivative h -> q(graphPoint h (Dv(x) h))
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometric equivalence of R^{n+l}, v : R^n -> R^l, y in R^{n+l} and U an open subset of R^n. If v is C^1 on U, then Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)) is C^1 on U, and for every x in U and h in R^n, fderiv Psi x h = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Amb n ℓ) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 v U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x => y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) U ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ h : Rn n, fderiv ℝ (fun x => y + q (graphPoint x (v x))) x h = q (graphPoint h (fderiv ℝ v x h))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^{n+l} -> R^n x R^l, Mathlib's canonical continuous linear equivalence (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean:378) sending z to the pair (first n coordinates of z, last l coordinates of z), i.e. (E z).1 i = z(Fin.castAdd l i) and (E z).2 j = z(Fin.natAdd n j). Let Psi(x) := y + q(graphPoint x (v x)). Hypotheses: q is a linear isometric equivalence of R^{n+l}, U is open and v is C^1 on U.
Provenance: this is the chain-rule computation in step 8 of the parent regraph proof, together with its coordinate identity (i), which is proved here in step 1 because the parent's sibling lemma is not available to this node; nothing from the parent is assumed.
1. graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b) for all a in R^n and b in R^l. By definition graphPoint a b is the vector of R^{n+l} with coordinates Fin.append a b; its Fin.castAdd l i-th coordinate is a i and its Fin.natAdd n j-th coordinate is b j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence E(graphPoint a b) = (a, b) componentwise, and applying E^{-1} proves the claim. [Lean: apply E.injective; rw [ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]; ext i <;> simp [graphPoint].]
2. Put L := q o E^{-1}, a continuous linear map R^n x R^l -> R^{n+l} (q is a linear isometry, hence continuous linear, and E^{-1} is continuous linear). By step 1, L(a, b) = q(graphPoint a b) for all a, b; hence Psi(x) = y + L(x, v x) for every x in R^n.
3. Psi is C^1 on U. The map x -> (x, v x) is C^1 on U because both components are: the identity is C^infinity and v is C^1 on U (ContDiffOn.prodMk). Composing with the continuous linear map L, which is C^infinity (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn), and adding the constant y (contDiffOn_const.add) preserves C^1 on U. By step 2 the resulting map is Psi.
4. The derivative. Fix x in U. Since U is open and v is C^1 on U with 1 != 0, v is differentiable at x, i.e. v has derivative Dv := fderiv v x at x. Hence x' -> (x', v x') has derivative h -> (h, Dv h) at x (HasFDerivAt.prodMk of hasFDerivAt_id and the derivative of v). A continuous linear map is its own derivative, so by the chain rule x' -> L(x', v x') has derivative h -> L(h, Dv h) at x, and adding the constant y does not change the derivative (HasFDerivAt.const_add). Therefore fderiv Psi x is the map h -> L(h, Dv h), and by step 2, fderiv Psi x h = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h)) for every h in R^n.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint a b = E^{-1}(a, b) for E = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd, checked coordinatewise via Fin.append
Psi(x) = y + L(x, v x) with L := q o E^{-1} continuous linear
C^1 on U: compose the C^1 map x -> (x, v x) with L and add the constant y
Chain rule at x in U: Psi has derivative h -> L(h, Dv(x) h) = q(graphPoint h (fderiv v x h))

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and includes all hypotheses. The proof independently establishes the graphPoint coordinate identity from Fin.append, so the empty dependency list is correct. It uses finAddEquivProd only as a continuous linear equivalence, then obtains C¹ regularity by composition and the exact derivative formula by the product and chain rules. Openness supplies ordinary differentiability at each specified point. No parent or unavailable sibling theorem is used.
